{% raw %}
`halt`: stop the computer, turning it off.

## Synopsis

<strong>halt</strong>

## Description

<strong>halt</strong> flushes its output and asks the kernel to turn the system off, as <strong>poweroff</strong>(1) does. Every process ends and its open files are closed, so what was written reaches the disks; then the machine turns off. Arguments are ignored.

To start again, use the power button, or <strong>reboot</strong>(1) instead.

## Exit status

On success <strong>halt</strong> does not return. If the kernel refuses, it prints the reason on standard error and exits with 1.

## Notes

Linux's <strong>halt</strong> stops the CPUs and leaves the power on. This computer's board has no such state: a CPU stops with its power on only after a fault, and a fault turns the machine off (its power light blinking amber; why is in <em>/sys/firmware/last\_shutdown</em> after the next boot). So <strong>halt</strong> powers off, as <strong>halt -p</strong> does.

## See also

<strong>poweroff</strong>(1), <strong>reboot</strong>(1), <strong>kill</strong>(1)
